preconditions.description: The number of test cases T is between 1 and 1000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= N <= 10**5 for N, K, S in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the length of the string N is between 1 and 100000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= K <= N for N, K, S in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the number of partitions K is between 1 and N inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(S.islower() and S.isalpha() for N, K, S in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the string S contains only lowercase Latin letters.

preconditions.expression: sum(N for N, K, S in test_cases) <= 2 * 10**5
preconditions.description: The sum of the lengths of all strings S across all test cases does not exceed 200000.

postconditions.expression: all(len(S_prime) == N for (N, K, S), S_prime in zip(test_cases, S_primes))
postconditions.description: The length of the output string S' is equal to the length of the input string S for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(S_prime.islower() and S_prime.isalpha() for S_prime in S_primes)
postconditions.description: The output string S' contains only lowercase Latin letters for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(S_prime == ''.join(sorted(S)) if K == 1 else S_prime == ''.join(sorted(''.join(partition) for partition in partitions)) for (N, K, S), S_prime, partitions in zip(test_cases, S_primes, partitions_list))
postconditions.description: The output string S' is the lexicographically smallest string that can be created by partitioning S into K non-empty subsequences and concatenating them.
